r: Best current broad 1.20.1 mod-compatibility starting point if you want a vanilla-ish world.

Direct hit for ugly modded magical flowers. Install this before trying to tolerate Botania/MythicBotany defaults.
If BOP is in your pack, this is one of the biggest single wins for making modded nature look intentional.
Best Excalibur-side fix for Create visual mismatch; excellent for a huge Forge 1.20.1 pack.
Very high fit for your pack because Apotheosis is already a major component and this removes its visual island.
Excellent companion for modded decoration-heavy worlds; very current 1.20.1 release.

n: Excalibur | Hearth and Harvest Delight Support
r: One of the prettiest verified 1.20.1 crop upgrades I found; ideal if Hearth and Harvest is in your pack.
Very complete Delight-family visual support; great for food-heavy packs.
Useful bridge if your pack combines Quark, Quark Delight and Farmer’s Delight.
Not a flower fix, but an excellent final polish layer if you want Excalibur and modern animated mobs together.
Choose this if you want the world prettier without pushing every mod into a radically different art direction.
My strongest “make the entire giant pack feel like one game” option. It wins through its active support-pack ecosystem.
Keep this in the catalogue because current Excalibur animation/compat instructions specifically call it out for 1.20.1.
If you use shaders/PBR, this can make Farmer’s Delight crops and kitchen blocks look dramatically less flat without a full medieval restyle.
If your main complaint is ugly flowers, use this as a reference for the kind of palette/model quality your modded-flower packs should match.
Use as a visual quality benchmark; not my first pick for a gigantic modded pack because direct mod coverage is weaker.
Strong cozy/rustic option, but weaker than Stay True/Excalibur for your “support lots of mods” goal.
Great if building textures are your priority, but not a broad mod-support leader.
Good if you want higher-res vanilla, but do not assume the famous Modded pack works on 1.20.1.
Coverage king historically. Keep as inspiration for what a modern 1.20.1 mega-pack should become, not as an install recommendation.
Still a useful aesthetic reference, but not where I would start a 1.20.1 mega-pack in 2026.
Useful for studying a curated mod-support ecosystem; not an install candidate for 1.20.1.
Exactly the kind of crop treatment you want, but the published pack is too old. Use Hearth & Harvest Excalibur or SPBR for current 1.20.1 instead.

Excellent “glue” pack for huge exploration packs: it fixes transitions rather than retexturing every asset.

n: JS Leaves+ for Biomes O’ Plenty
v: Maybe via broad tags; not exact stable-file verified
r: Visually gorgeous for BOP foliage, but the current files are centered on 1.21.x; test before relying on it in 1.20.1.

Small scope but exactly the kind of quality-of-life visual fix you asked for: it turns Quark glowshroom into a proper 3D model on 1.20.1.
Not related to flowers, but one of the highest-value visual layers once block/plant texture consistency is solved.
Use only after the core Fresh Animations stack is stable.

n: Iron’s Botany — dedicated texture pack gap
r: Use Fresh MythicBotany & Botania + an Iron’s Spells support pack now, but the remaining Iron’s Botany-owned textures are a prime candidate for us to make a small dedicated 1.20.1 resource pack.

n: Stay True Compats Reforged — Farmer’s Delight lane
r: You do not need a second Stay True-specific Farmer’s Delight pack to get baseline compatibility; start with Compats Reforged, then layer a more specialized crop pack only if desired.

n: Stay True Compats Reforged — Biomes O’ Plenty lane
r: Use this as the baseline BOP integration; Retextures o’ Plenty can then sit above it if you prefer its stronger BOP-specific redesign.

n: Stay True Compats Reforged — Create lane
r: Best if you want Create to remain vanilla-ish rather than switching to Excalibur’s medieval machinery style.

n: Stay True Compats Reforged — Quark lane
r: Useful for large packs because Quark touches a huge number of world-facing blocks.
